classification: identifiable artificial spillway / Great Falls upper approach
finding: The line crosses the upper curved spillway/forebay outlet visible just north of the road bridge, then follows the wetted approach toward the natural falls. No upward bridge-deck spike. The 100 m screening drop includes both the outlet and sloping approach, so it is not a dam-height measurement.

classification: same upper approach; no independent waterfall identified
finding: Window lies on the sloping rocky/wetted approach between the upper outlet and Great Falls crest. It overlaps the approach signal of C01; manually grouped with that approach, rather than counted as another waterfall.

classification: known natural waterfall: Paterson Great Falls
finding: Screening rediscovers the original falls within 1 m of the 500 m reference. Route follows 6DM6E over the falls; the eastern power-channel branch remains rejected. Original first 1,001 values are identical. NPS 77 ft remains distinct from this local DEM estimate.

classification: broad downstream DEM gradient; independent waterfall unconfirmed
finding: A low gradient below the chasm, next to the eastern riverside building. Centerline remains in the river. Lateral checks closely agree. No discrete cross-channel barrier or separate falling ledge is established by the image. Water-surface interpolation in the DEM remains a possible influence.

classification: broad DEM decline near a bridge; waterfall unconfirmed
finding: The screened window spans the river around a road crossing. The curve is a broad decline over roughly 80 m, not a sharp vertical ledge. There is no positive bridge-height spike, and ±5 m profiles agree. No separate waterfall or dam is identifiable; do not interpret 0.806 m as a waterfall height.

classification: subthreshold context check; smooth river DEM gradient
finding: Strongest 100 m decline beyond 2,000 m, but only about 0.11 m. Image shows the route in the main river away from the adjacent street and banks. No discrete fall or dam established; no animation stop.

classification: subthreshold context check; smooth river DEM gradient
finding: Second separated downstream context check selected beyond 2,000 m. River centerline remains in the wetted channel, clear of the nearby bridge in this 100 m window. Smooth decline, no discrete waterfall established; no animation stop.
